gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Noto Sans Mandaic has curvy, loose letters whose lowercase climbs nearly to the capitals, while Quilon above it swells and thins with an editorial hand. Pages stay easy going.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Quilon is a display face with a subtle weight gradient along every curve and a commanding editorial air. Noto Sans Meetei Mayek goes quieter, its low-contrast rounds gapped like a cracked bangle.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-mende-kikakui: A gentle swell and thinning of stroke gives Quilon its commanding, editorial look at display sizes. And Noto Sans Mende Kikakui backs it up with low contrast and daylight through every curved opening.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Quilon is a display face whose bowls thin gracefully rather than sharply, which suits big, short lines. And Noto Sans Meroitic stays low in contrast, with see-through openings and lowercase filling the line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Quilon keeps its stems only a shade heavier than the arms joining them, giving a commanding editorial display look, while Noto Sans Ogham sits underneath with tall, bold-looking lowercase. Paragraphs move along briskly.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-hungarian: Wide, generous counters in tall a, e and s give Quilon its display presence, with shading that moves across both round and straight strokes. Noto Sans Old Hungarian can go small, since its apertures stay open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Quilon is an editorial display face, its thin strokes dipping only modestly as they thin out. Noto Sans Old Italic supplies the strongest quality: lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals, curve endings kept well apart.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Noto Sans Old Permic has rounded forms that stay open to the side, and lowercase nearly matching its capitals in height. And Quilon above it, with thinner joins where curves meet stems, feels commanding against that softness.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Thick strokes that lead the eye without bullying it. Quilon brings that editorial confidence, and Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong lets it breathe beside low-contrast rounds that gap like a cracked bangle under a high-set x-height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans PhagsPa, with see-through openings and a gentle bump up to capitals. Quilon is the commanding editorial voice, bending its strokes with a mild taper.
